paper.title: Revisiting Projection-free Online Learning: the Strongly Convex Case

settings.name_in_paper: Online convex optimization with full information, strongly convex losses (projection-free)
unmapped: the learner knows the outer radius R of the feasible set (r B ⊆ K ⊆ R B)
losses bounded by M in sup-norm (|f_t| <= M), subgradients bounded by G
settings.definition_quote: an online learner is required to iteratively choose actions from a fixed feasible set $\mK\subseteq\reals^n$ which is assumed convex and compact. After choosing his action $\x_t\in\mK$ on round $t\in[T]$ ($T$ is assumed to be known beforehand), the learner observes a loss function $f_t(\cdot)$, which is chosen by an adversary

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit convex optimization, strongly convex losses (projection-free)
unmapped: the learner knows the outer radius R of the feasible set (r B ⊆ K ⊆ R B)
the learner knows the loss bound M (|f_t| <= M) when using the tuned c
settings.definition_quote: In the bandit-information setting, instead of observing the loss function after each iteration, the learner only observes his loss, that is the scalar value $f_t(\x_t)$. In this setting, we assume the adversary is oblivious, i.e., the loss functions $f_1,\dots,f_T$ are chosen beforehand and do not depend on the actions of the learner.
